name: United States
summary: Home to Miami, the launch gateway of Monumental Streams, and to New York City, a stop on the opening WAVEMAKERS journey.

name: Florida
summary: US state at the meeting point of the Caribbean, Latin America and North America; home to Miami-Dade County.

name: Miami-Dade County
summary: The county that contains both the City of Miami and the separate City of Miami Beach, along with dozens of other municipalities.

name: Miami
summary: The launch focus of Monumental Streams and its opening gateway into the wider world. The City of Miami, incorporated in 1896, sits on Biscayne Bay; it is a separate city from Miami Beach, which lies across the bay on barrier islands.

facts.label: Incorporated
facts.value: 28 July 1896

facts.label: Railway
facts.value: Henry Flagler's Florida East Coast Railway reached Miami in April 1896, months before incorporation

facts.label: Not Miami Beach
facts.value: Miami Beach is a separate city in Miami-Dade County, across Biscayne Bay

name: Wynwood
summary: A Miami neighbourhood just north of downtown. Once a warehouse and garment district with a large Puerto Rican community, it became known from the late 2000s for large-scale murals, galleries and studios.

facts.label: Wynwood Walls
facts.value: Outdoor mural project founded in 2009 by developer Tony Goldman

facts.label: Mid-20th century
facts.value: Home to a large Puerto Rican community

name: Little Havana
summary: A Miami neighbourhood west of downtown, centred on SW 8th Street, known as Calle Ocho. It became the heart of Cuban exile life after 1959 and is now home to people from across Latin America.

facts.label: Main street
facts.value: SW 8th Street, known as Calle Ocho

facts.label: Landmark
facts.value: Máximo Gómez Park, known as Domino Park, on Calle Ocho

name: Little Haiti
summary: A Miami neighbourhood north of the Design District and the centre of Haitian life in South Florida since the 1970s and 1980s. Its area overlaps the historic settlement of Lemon City, which predates the City of Miami.

name: Overtown
summary: One of Miami's oldest neighbourhoods, just northwest of downtown. Founded as 'Colored Town' under segregation, it grew into a centre of Black business and nightlife nicknamed the 'Harlem of the South', before 1960s interstate construction displaced much of its community.

facts.label: Historic name
facts.value: Colored Town, the name used under segregation

facts.label: Lyric Theater
facts.value: Opened in 1913 on NW 2nd Avenue
facts.source: Black Archives History & Research Foundation of South Florida

facts.label: Highways
facts.value: Construction of I-95 and I-395 in the 1960s displaced much of the neighbourhood's population

name: Brickell
summary: Miami's financial district, a dense run of high-rise towers south of the Miami River. Mapped for future stories.

name: Downtown Miami
summary: The city's historic core and civic centre on Biscayne Bay. Mapped for future stories.

name: Allapattah
summary: A Miami neighbourhood west of Wynwood with a large Dominican community and a long-standing produce-market district. Mapped for future stories.

name: Coconut Grove
summary: One of the oldest settled areas of Miami, on Biscayne Bay, annexed by the city in 1925. Its West Grove was settled in the late 19th century by Bahamian workers. Mapped for future stories.

name: Miami Design District
summary: A Miami neighbourhood of design showrooms, galleries and fashion houses, north of Wynwood. Mapped for future stories.

name: Miami Beach
summary: A separate city from Miami, on barrier islands across Biscayne Bay, incorporated in 1915. Its South Beach neighbourhood holds the Miami Beach Architectural District, one of the best-known concentrations of Art Deco buildings in the world.

facts.label: Incorporated
facts.value: 26 March 1915

facts.label: Not the City of Miami
facts.value: Miami Beach is its own municipality in Miami-Dade County

name: South Beach
summary: The southern part of the City of Miami Beach, home to Ocean Drive, Lincoln Road and most of the Art Deco district.

name: Miami Beach Architectural District
summary: The historic district, usually called the Art Deco District, covering much of South Beach in the City of Miami Beach. Its hotels and apartment buildings, built mostly between 1923 and 1943, mix Mediterranean Revival, Art Deco and Streamline Moderne styles.

facts.label: National Register
facts.value: Listed on the US National Register of Historic Places in 1979
facts.source: US National Register of Historic Places

facts.label: Campaign
facts.value: Listing followed a campaign by the Miami Design Preservation League, founded in 1976

name: Coral Gables
summary: A separate city in Miami-Dade County, southwest of Miami, planned by George Merrick in the 1920s and incorporated in 1925. Known for its Mediterranean Revival streets, the Venetian Pool, the Miracle Mile and the main campus of the University of Miami.

name: Key Biscayne
summary: An island across Biscayne Bay from Miami, reached by the Rickenbacker Causeway. Its municipality is a village, incorporated in 1991; the island is also home to Crandon Park and Bill Baggs Cape Florida State Park.

name: Brevard County
summary: A county on Florida's Atlantic coast, far north of Miami, home to Cape Canaveral and NASA's Kennedy Space Center on Merritt Island.

name: Kennedy Space Center Launch Complex 39A
summary: A launch pad at NASA's Kennedy Space Center on Merritt Island, Brevard County, Florida (not Miami). Apollo 11 lifted off from here on 16 July 1969.

facts.label: Apollo 11
facts.value: Launched from Pad 39A on 16 July 1969

name: Puerto Rico
summary: An unincorporated territory of the United States in the Caribbean; Puerto Ricans have been US citizens since 1917. Home of bomba, plena and reggaeton, and the starting point of the opening WAVEMAKERS chapter.

name: San Juan
summary: The capital and largest city of Puerto Rico, founded by Spanish colonists in 1521. The journey of the opening WAVEMAKERS chapter begins here.

facts.label: World Heritage
facts.value: La Fortaleza and San Juan National Historic Site, inscribed in 1983

name: Old San Juan
summary: The walled colonial quarter on San Juan islet, guarded by the fortresses of El Morro and San Cristóbal. Mapped for future stories.

name: Santurce
summary: A district of San Juan and a hub for contemporary art and music, home to the Museo de Arte de Puerto Rico and the Plaza del Mercado.

name: Loíza
summary: A coastal municipality east of San Juan and a heartland of Afro-Puerto Rican culture, where the bomba tradition runs especially deep.

facts.label: Festival
facts.value: Fiestas de Santiago Apóstol, held each July, known for vejigante masks

facts.label: Tradition
facts.value: One of the best-known centres of bomba music and dance

name: Ponce
summary: A city on Puerto Rico's southern coast, where plena is traced to working-class neighbourhoods around 1900.

name: New York
summary: US state that contains New York City.

name: New York City
summary: The second stop on the opening WAVEMAKERS journey: destination of the Puerto Rican Great Migration, birthplace of hip hop and home of New York salsa.

name: The Bronx
summary: New York City's northernmost borough and the only one mainly on the mainland, widely recognised as the birthplace of hip hop.

facts.label: Hip hop
facts.value: DJ Kool Herc's party at 1520 Sedgwick Avenue on 11 August 1973 is widely cited as hip hop's starting point
facts.source: Smithsonian National Museum of African American History and Culture

facts.label: Geography
facts.value: The only New York City borough located mainly on the US mainland

name: Manhattan
summary: New York City's central borough, home to East Harlem and the Lower East Side, two centres of Puerto Rican New York.

name: Brooklyn
summary: New York City's most populous borough, home to Coney Island.

name: East Harlem
summary: A neighbourhood in northeast Manhattan, known as Spanish Harlem or El Barrio, and a centre of Puerto Rican life in New York since the early 20th century.

name: Lower East Side
summary: A historic immigrant neighbourhood in lower Manhattan. Its Puerto Rican community named the blocks around the lettered avenues 'Loisaida', and it is home to the Nuyorican Poets Café.

name: Coney Island
summary: Brooklyn's seaside neighbourhood of boardwalk and amusement parks. By 1905, Luna Park and Dreamland lit it up at night with electric light.

name: 1520 Sedgwick Avenue
summary: An apartment building in the Morris Heights section of the Bronx. On 11 August 1973, DJ Kool Herc played a back-to-school party in its recreation room that is widely cited as the birth of hip hop.

name: United Kingdom
summary: Home to London, the final stop on the opening WAVEMAKERS journey.

name: England
summary: The largest of the four countries of the United Kingdom.

name: London
summary: The final stop on the opening WAVEMAKERS journey: shaped by the Windrush generation, carnival, sound systems, lovers rock and grime.

name: Brixton
summary: A South London neighbourhood in the borough of Lambeth and a centre of Caribbean life in Britain since the Windrush era.

facts.label: Windrush Square
facts.value: Named in 1998 to mark fifty years since the arrival of the Empire Windrush

facts.label: Black Cultural Archives
facts.value: Opened its home on Windrush Square in 2014

name: Notting Hill
summary: A West London neighbourhood in Kensington and Chelsea, home of the Notting Hill Carnival over the August bank holiday weekend.

facts.value: Scene of the Notting Hill race riots

facts.label: Carnival
facts.value: First held as an outdoor street event in 1966

name: Bow
summary: An East London district in Tower Hamlets, closely tied to the birth of grime; Wiley and Dizzee Rascal both came from Bow.

name: Tottenham
summary: A North London district in Haringey and a major grime hub, where Skepta and JME grew up.

name: Jamaica
summary: Caribbean island nation whose sound systems and music reshaped culture in New York, London and beyond.

name: Kingston
summary: Jamaica's capital, where sound-system culture took shape in the 1950s, followed by ska, rocksteady, reggae and dub.

name: Cuba
summary: Caribbean island nation, about 90 miles from Key West; exile after the 1959 revolution remade Miami.

name: Havana
summary: Cuba's capital, from which many exiles left for Miami after 1959.

name: Mariel
summary: A port town west of Havana, the departure point of the 1980 Mariel boatlift.

name: Haiti
summary: Caribbean nation sharing the island of Hispaniola; Haitian migration built Miami's Little Haiti.

name: Port-au-Prince
summary: Haiti's capital.

name: Netherlands
summary: Country in northwestern Europe, mapped for the films shot in Amsterdam.

name: Amsterdam
summary: Capital of the Netherlands. The Blender Foundation's open movie Tears of Steel was shot here, including at the medieval Oude Kerk.

name: Japan
summary: Mapped for expansion. No stories yet.

name: Tokyo
summary: Japan's capital. Mapped for expansion; no stories yet.

name: Brazil
summary: Mapped for expansion. No stories yet.

name: Rio de Janeiro
summary: Brazilian city on Guanabara Bay. Mapped for expansion; no stories yet.

name: Nigeria
summary: Mapped for expansion. No stories yet.

name: Lagos
summary: Nigeria's largest city. Mapped for expansion; no stories yet.

name: South Korea
summary: Mapped for expansion. No stories yet.

name: Seoul
summary: South Korea's capital. Mapped for expansion; no stories yet.

name: Mexico
summary: Mapped for expansion. No stories yet.

name: Mexico City
summary: Mexico's capital. Mapped for expansion; no stories yet.

name: Washington, D.C.
summary: The capital of the United States — a federal district, not part of any state.

name: Griffith Stadium
summary: Ballpark in Washington, D.C., home of the Washington Senators; demolished in 1965.

name: The Hague
summary: Dutch seat of government on the North Sea coast, with dunes along its shore.

name: California
summary: US state on the Pacific coast.

name: Los Angeles
summary: Southern California city and home of the Hollywood film industry.

name: Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum
summary: Stadium in Exposition Park, Los Angeles; the Dodgers played there before Dodger Stadium opened in 1962.

name: Hollywood
summary: Los Angeles neighbourhood synonymous with the American film industry.

name: Queens
summary: New York City borough on Long Island.

name: Flushing Meadows–Corona Park
summary: Park in Queens that hosted the 1939–40 and 1964–65 New York World’s Fairs.

name: Buckingham Palace
summary: The London residence of the British monarch.

name: Portsmouth
summary: Port city on England’s south coast.

name: Cape Canaveral launch site
summary: Rocket launch site on Florida’s Atlantic coast, today Cape Canaveral Space Force Station — not Miami.

name: Italy
summary: Country in southern Europe.

name: Rome
summary: Capital of Italy, home of the Trevi Fountain and the Roman Forum.

name: Vondelpark
summary: Amsterdam’s best-known city park.
